text:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — billing flagged a reserved SKU mismatch in ap-southeast. Our 2-week forecast shows tail spikes that could push us ~12% over committed GPUs during peak nights. Can someone triage? cc @tess @elaine

elaine: On it. Do we have the export? rough numbers pls.

sanjay: From the demand model (rolling 7d):
```
committed_gpus: 120
forecast_peak_gpu_demand: 135
expected_spill_hours: 52
est_extra_cost_if_on_demand: $19,800
prob_tail_spike (>12%): 0.28
```
I also saw a billing line: 'GPU_COMMITTED_SKU_V2' vs 'GPU_COMMITTED_SKU' — looks like provider changed sku mapping; could cause double billing.

mike: If tail is real, quick options:
- spin up limited preemptible pool to absorb 8-12 GPUs overnight
- adjust routing to prefer cached KV for gen-heavy endpoints
- request short-term capacity swap with provider (ask for 2-week exchange)
I'll test a preemptible rollout in staging.

tess (finance): We already have a pending invoice variance — devops flagged $12k credit earlier this month that didn't reconcile. If SKUs remapped we'll either see a credit or an extra charge. Filing a billing ticket with provider now. Need timeline for infra changes.

hana: Routing change might be safest short-term. We can throttle lower-priority customers during 00:00-06:00 UTC and redirect to smaller models for non-SLA tenants. That buys time.

infra-bot: alert created: INC-4567 — reserved-sku-mismatch-ap-southeast. Assigned: eng-infra. Priority: high.

elaine: Action plan proposal:
1) mike to spin preemptible 10 GPUs (nightly, 00:00-08:00 UTC) — test by EOD
2) hana to add soft throttles for tier-2 customers (gradual ramp) — start tomorrow
3) tess to open official billing dispute + share invoice lines
4) sanjay to update forecast with tail volatility factor +0.12 and re-run
I'll consolidate in the capacity spreadsheet.

mike: :thumbsup: I'll have a terraform diff in #eng-infra-deploy in ~2 hours.

tess (finance): Opened ticket with provider — ref PROD-78921. Asked for SKU mapping and any auto-migration credits. cc @mike

sanjay: :eyes: Thanks. If provider can't give swap, we should consider increasing committed by 12 GPUs for Q next commit window — need cost calc.

hana: I'll sketch throttle banding policy and share a small eval script to measure user impact.

mike: quick note — preemptible will reduce cost but increases tail risk for long-running pipelines; we'll limit to gen-only endpoints.

sanjay: Great. Thanks everyone. Please update INC-4567 with progress. I'll loop in product if this looks like a recurring tail risk.
